I tumori del cardias e del fondo sono pi:
Tumors of the cardia and fundus are harder to see than those of the antrum: the cardia is often poorly distended and the wall near the gastroesophageal junction can look normally thicker. Clues to disease: asymmetric solid tissue, heterogeneous enhancement, narrowed lumen, irregular outer contour.
For tumors near the gastroesophageal junction, the distance from the junction matters (Siewert classification): tumors whose center is within 2 cm of the junction and involve it are staged as esophageal, the others as gastric. CT estimates it, but endoscopy decides.
In staging: liver, peritoneum (ascites, omental nodules), lymph nodes along the left gastric artery, the celiac trunk and the splenic artery, and the spleen and pancreatic tail, which a fundal tumor can invade (T4b). CT underestimates lymph nodes and peritoneum.
Al cardias un tessuto solido asimmetrico: At the cardia, asymmetric enhancing solid tissue is not "poor distension": send for endoscopy.
Adenocarcinoma gastrico del fondo, G3, p: Gastric adenocarcinoma of the fundus, G3, pT4a pN1 (1 positive lymph node out of 7), pathologic stage IIIA (AJCC 8th ed.), maximum diameter 5 cm, R0 resection (GDC clinical data from the CPTAC-STAD collection).
